title: This Fish Shoots Down Insects and Fixes Light's Lie First
subject: archerfish

scenes.text: A fish hunts insects above the water. Water bends light, so it should miss.
The archerfish spits a jet that can reach two meters, though it is only about a foot long.
At the surface, light bends and shifts where prey looks by up to 25 degrees.
So before it fires, the fish changes the angle of its jet to correct for it.
It also tunes the force from 40 to 500 millinewtons to match the size of the prey.
Young fish improve by watching others spit. A practiced fish hits targets within 65 centimeters every time.

description:
An archerfish shoots insects off branches with a jet of water.
It corrects for light bending at the surface and tunes the force of each shot.
